chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Sindi ibn Muhammad from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar from Muhammad al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When silver exceeds two hundred dirhams by forty dirhams, one dirham is due in it, and there is nothing due for less than forty. I asked, 'What is due for thirty-nine dirhams?' He said, 'There is nothing due for thirty-nine dirhams.'

key_terms.أَرْبَعُونَ دِرْهَمًا: Forty dirhams (the increment for zakat liability)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of silver required to pay zakat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific calculation of silver zakat, establishing that the full rate applies once the holding exceeds 200 dirhams by at least 40, while smaller increments above the base threshold remain exempt. This detail highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise quantitative thresholds (nisab) in financial jurisprudence, distinguishing it from other schools that may apply proportional rates for smaller amounts. The hadith underscores the principle that zakat is a fixed obligation triggered by reaching specific cumulative milestones rather than a continuous sliding scale for minor surpluses.
